analysis: Integration pass over 36 units. Changes: (a) in-memory PromptTokenCache (PromptTokenCache.swift) reusing chat-template piece token IDs, keyed by SHA-256 over a domain tag, length-prefixed scope and piece bytes, so a different scope cannot hit another scope's entries. Memory-only, bounded (32 MiB default, 4096 MiB cap, per-entry cap capacity/8), with load-time self-check, sampled background verification and a kill switch. The scheduler passes promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil (MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift ~833-835), the coordinator-authored scope per T-041. The new hit/miss timing difference stays within one scope, the accepted same-account SEC-035 channel. No at-rest artifact, so T-041 leak #2 is untouched. (b) ChatTemplateLoopRewrites does exact-match string rewrites that fail safe to nil. (c) decodeInboundChatRequest merges the decode passes; reserved tool-schema metadata rejection still precedes it, with no modelType passed (same as the old handler call) and no prompt-content logging. (d) Cold-load work-FIFO release (ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift, Serve.swift). Only inferenceRequest, cancel, attestationChallenge, codeAttestationResumeChallenge and runtimeOutdated overtake. connected, disconnected, trustStatus, appAttestShadow, drainAck and model-management events wait. Cancel is deferred and applied on admission return. Registration and cancel ownership exist before release. App Attest connection control stays on the separate eventTask reader. (e) LaunchAgent passthrough adds five fixed allowlisted TTFT env keys; the operator is already the TB-003 adversary. (f) Jinja sanitizer leaf fast path preserves output. (g) The --prompt-prep benchmark uses synthetic data, is local only, and touches no serving path. Everything else is tests and docs. I found no concrete regression. Residual unverified items: the source supplying promptCacheScope in PromptTokenCache.tokenize (it must be the coordinator cacheSalt, with nil or empty never collapsing to a shared scope); whether LocalTokenizerLoader now bypassing AutoTokenizer changes tokenization for all models (the self-check compares against the same upstream object); whether grant, revocation and connection checks (T-053) are re-applied after a released load wait; and whether ReleasedAdmission entries are always cleaned up. The threat model should mention the prompt-token cache under T-041/A-001.
